models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B Instruct (MLX INT4, group 64)

measured.source: this port, four readings, one on battery and three on AC; long-synthesis spans 14% here and is what sets the oracle floor

models.notes: The install every frozen Gemma 4 row in docs/BENCHMARKS.md is measured against, and the one the sensitivity proof and the mlx-lm cross-engine KL run on. If you install one model, install this one.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B (MLX INT4, group 64)

measured.source: this port, two readings, AC; the slowest case agrees to 0.13 tok/s across them

models.notes: Gated-DeltaNet linear attention on 30 of 40 layers. One of the two gated rows with NO cross-engine KL number (qwen38-27b is the other): scripts/kld.py is still pinned to a Gemma reference repo, so nothing external has checked this family's numerics.

models.name: Qwen3-30B-A3B (GGUF Q4_K_M)

measured.source: this port, one oracle reading, AC

models.notes: 128 experts of 2.5 MiB, so it streams. Peak footprint 2.7 GiB rather than the README band: 48 layers deep, and the slot cache is slots x layers x expert_stride.

models.name: gpt-oss 20B (GGUF MXFP4)

measured.source: this port, two readings, AC; the first had a release build running beside it and is ~7% low on the shortest case

models.notes: Harmony puts reasoning in an analysis channel BEFORE the answer, so turbospark-check prints the answer on stdout and the reasoning on stderr. Needs an 8192 context AND a 3072-token budget: its three protocol cases take 818 / 2153 / 1108 tokens to reach the stop token. Peak footprint 5,421 MiB, most of it expert-slot cache.

models.name: Ternary-Bonsai 27B (MLX affine 2-bit, group 128)
models.notes: Dense, so it streams nothing and its counted footprint is 661.6 MiB on 7.6 GB of weights -- but a dense model's weights are mapped and NOT counted, so budget its size on disk in free RAM. Ships merges.txt and NO generation_config.json, the exact inverse of qwen38-27b.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B (MLX INT4, group 64)

measured.source: this port, three readings, AC; two from turbospark-bench and one from the oracle

models.notes: Same architecture as ternary27b and bonsai27b, at a third quantization. Renders in NON-THINKING mode, so the shared 1024-token budget is enough. No merges.txt: this conversion embeds the merges in tokenizer.json. Has no cross-engine KL number (see qwen36).

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B (MLX INT4, group 64) + MTP head
models.notes: Same trunk as qwen38-27b (mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit, byte-identical), plus its multi-token-prediction head streamed from the official Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B repo's last shard and quantized to INT4 group 64 here at repack time -- that conversion drops the head, so it can only be read off the original checkpoint (docs/MTP.md, docs/MTP_SPECULATIVE.md step 1). Speculation is off unless asked for (--speculative auto|N, --speculative-drafter mtp); with it off this install is provably inert against qwen38-27b, same perplexity and both frozen digests. Measured block-2 accept length 1.84/round, 1.44x end to end on the clock (docs/MTP.md); no dedicated memory-oracle or quality-gate row of its own, since qwen38_memory_oracle and qwen38_quality_gate already pin the shared trunk.

models.name: Qwen3.8 27B (MLX INT4, group 64) with vision tower

measured.source: this port, one reading, AC, four rounds of image transcription at varying page sizes

models.notes: A THIRD entry for this same repo and revision, deliberately kept separate from qwen38-27b: that row backs qwen38_memory_oracle and qwen38_quality_gate's frozen numbers, and adding ~0.9 GiB of vision tower to it would force a re-freeze for a component neither gate exercises. Streamed WITH vision_tower.* included (crates/repack/tests/qwen38_checkpoint_network.rs's vision-carrying test), where the plain row's install excludes it. The decode_tok_s_min reading is the FIRST of four rounds, a cold-GPU forward pass (AGENTS.md Gotcha 20), not the largest page -- the repeated large-page round later in the same run reads faster (15.997) than either smaller page. See docs/VISION.md.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B Instruct (GGUF UD-Q3_K_M, IQ3_XXS/IQ4_NL experts)
models.notes: -20% expert bytes against the MLX INT4 install for +2.56% perplexity (38.3753 against 37.4176), and it decodes SLOWER: 22.9-25.4 tok/s on the protocol against 35-41, at 2.0-2.4x the joules per token. A memory result, not a speed or power one.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B Instruct (GGUF Q8_0)
models.notes: Eight bits and MEASURABLY WORSE than the INT4 MLX install on this corpus (perplexity 39.88 against 37.42), confirmed against llama.cpp on the identical bytes. Do not assume more bits is better here.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B (GGUF Q4_K_M)
models.notes: The mixed-block-type case: Q4_K experts and embedding, Q8_0 attention, one Q6_K tensor. The walk un-does llama.cpp's V-head interleaving on eight tensors; five of them are quantized and no BF16 probe can see them.

models.name: Ornith-1.5 35B-A3B (MLX INT4, group 64)

measured.source: this port, two readings (bench + memory oracle), AC; peaks span 1570.6-1578.5 MiB across six cases

models.notes: A retrain of Qwen 3.6's architecture: its config derives qwen_gdn_moe_35b_a3b() field for field from BOTH the HF config and llama.cpp's GGUF metadata independently, so no ArchConfig, kernel or flow work was needed. 1.63-1.67x faster than the same model's Q8_0 GGUF install at half the expert stride. The publisher's own MLX conversion DROPS the mtp.* head, so this install clears speculation_blocker's dtype arm and still cannot draft. No cross-engine KL.

models.name: Ornith-1.5 35B-A3B (GGUF Q8_0)
models.notes: Superseded by `ornith35b` on every axis measured -- same model, 1.63-1.67x slower, twice the expert stride, twice the disk -- so it carries NO frozen row deliberately: what it is for is being the Q8_0 arm of that quantization A/B, which is throughput and needs no digest. Q8_0 rather than Q4_K_M for the same superblock-alignment reason as `ornith9b`. Headless: the walk skips the MTP block by name, since a head is ingested from safetensors rather than from a GGUF. Measured install 36,848,844,396 bytes, 953 MB UNDER the download: this is the first GGUF row here whose source declares a block the walk deliberately drops, and blk.40's 256 experts are most of the difference. install_bytes is declared at the download size, which the field's contract permits (generous only) and which a_gguf_rows_install_is_never_smaller_than_its_download requires.

models.name: Ornith-1.5 9B (GGUF Q8_0)

measured.source: this port, two readings (bench + memory oracle), AC; peaks span 434.9-438.4 MiB across six cases

models.notes: Q8_0 and NOT Q4_K_M, which is forced rather than preferred: this family's V-head de-interleave runs on the COLUMNS of linear_attn.out_proj, and a 128-column head is half a 256-element K-quant superblock, so the Q4_K_M file is refused by name. Nothing is given up -- the Q8_0 file is Q8_0 and F32 throughout. NO MTP head: this checkpoint publishes none, so it cannot speculate at any dtype. No cross-engine KL. Measured install 9,527,311,745 bytes, marginally UNDER the download because the walk narrows this file's 177 F32 tensors to BF16; install_bytes is declared at the download size, which the field's contract permits (generous only).

models.name: Bonsai 27B (MLX affine 1-bit, group 128)
models.notes: One bit. The cross-engine KL needs the PrismML mlx fork, because upstream mlx refuses bits=1 at the API level on every device. Has no quality-gate or memory-oracle row.

models.name: Mistral 7B Instruct v0.3 (GGUF Q4_K_M, dense)

measured.source: this port, two readings, AC; the slowest case moved 12.5% between them, which is why the floor came off the slower

models.notes: Dense, so nothing streams and there are zero packed-expert files. Its oracle runs at 8192 context, not the shared 4096: the protocol's long case is 3444 tokens under Mistral's 32k vocab and does not fit otherwise. Counted footprint 1,201 MiB at 8192 and 684 at 4096, of which KV is most -- the 4.07 GiB of weights are not counted, so budget disk size in free RAM.

models.name: TinyLlama 1.1B Chat v1.0 (GGUF Q6_K, dense)
models.notes: The cheapest real install here, ~3 minutes. Its chat framing is Zephyr and its special-token table is Mistral's, which is why framing comes from the checkpoint's own template and not from the dialect probe.

models.name: Mixtral 8x7B Instruct v0.1 (GGUF Q4_K_M)
models.notes: INSTALLS AND RUNS AND CANNOT STREAM USEFULLY. 8 experts of 108.9 MiB means 54.5 GiB of pinned slot cache at the default 16 slots; at slots == experts it pins the whole 27.2 GiB expert table, which is not streaming. Expert GRANULARITY decides what this engine can hold, not model size. Listed so the arithmetic is visible before the 26 GB download rather than after it.

models.name: Muse Glimmer 30B (MLX INT4, group 64)

measured.source: this port, one reading, AC; this install draws ~38 W and saturates thermally within ~2 minutes, so its rate is governed (AGENTS.md Gotcha 28)

models.notes: The seventh family and the sixth decode flow: dense 52-layer GQA with a three-sliding/one-full 2048 window, NoPE on the full layers, a separate attention output gate, CENTERED per-layer norms against a PLAIN final one, and a logit softcap behind an output multiplier. It REASONS BEFORE ANSWERING (a to=self message precedes its to=user one), so its protocol runs at 8,192 context and a 2,048 budget rather than the shared 4,096/1,024. A vision-language checkpoint whose text tower alone is ingested; its 815 vision tensors are excluded at repack.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next REAP-288 (MLX INT4)
models.notes: qwen4_exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), REAP-288 is a pruned-expert variant (288 of the original expert count) at top-10 routing. Window is capped at 2048: the checkpoint's own compressed_attention.index_budget, not a chosen number (docs/QWEN4_EXP.md, docs/QWEN4_PHASE0.md), so long-synthesis (2940 tokens under this vocab) cannot run and this row is not comparable to any other family's. Router and shared-expert-gate ship raw BF16 on this checkpoint rather than pre-packed U32 like every other MoE family here; both are force-quantized to INT8 at repack time (docs/QWEN4_EXP.md's dtype-bug fix). No quality-gate row yet: same-process repeated greedy generation at 2048 context does not reproduce (fresh-process greedy runs agree byte for byte; within-process reruns after a discarded warmup diverge), a real finding rather than a test-authoring gap, still open as of this row. No speculative drafter exists for this checkpoint (288 experts, no MTP-ingestible head in any published MLX conversion).
